instruction: In a new sheet, identify which year had the maximum Fixed Assets value and write both the year and the value in cells A2 and B2 respectively.

metadata.explanation: Task requires finding the maximum Fixed Assets value in column C. Verified with Python: max value is 45500 in year 2014. Evaluator checks new sheet (Sheet2) for year in column A and value in column B.

scoring_breakdown.1.0: Correct year and value both written to new sheet

llm_judge_reasons: CRITICAL: Getter logic is semantically incorrect - it scans all rows in column B to find maximum value, instead of directly reading cells A2 and B2 as the instruction requires

SEMANTIC MISMATCH: Instruction requires user to write year in A2 and value in B2, but getter searches for max value across column B (lines 42-49 in xlsx.py:8-56). This means if column B has any existing data or multiple values, the getter will read the wrong data
WRONG STATE EXTRACTION: Getter extracts 'year from row with max value in column B' instead of 'value written by user in cell A2'. These are semantically different verification targets
LOGIC CONFLICT: Getter re-calculates the maximum value instead of verifying what the user wrote. If user correctly writes 2014 and 45500 to A2/B2, but column B has other data, verification will fail
The getter should simply read ws['A2'].value and ws['B2'].value from Sheet2, not iterate through rows 2 to max_row looking for maximum
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Rewrite getter to directly read cells A2 and B2 from sheet index 1: return {'year': ws['A2'].value, 'value': ws['B2'].value}
Remove the max-finding loop (lines 42-49) since the user already identified and wrote the max value
Ensure the getter reads the NEW sheet (Sheet2, index 1) not the original data sheet
The expected values (year=2014, value=45500) are correct, but the getter extraction logic needs to be fixed to read the user's output cells, not recalculate the maximum
